title: Org-wide engineering sync — week of 2026-06-09
content:
Attendees: eng leads + SRE reps + product PMs (snapshot below)

Purpose: concise org-level summary for engineering — signals, tactical asks, and where we need cross-team attention this week. Save for the Monday all-hands follow-up and share links in #eng-org.

1) TL;DR highlights
- Runtime v1.12 canary started (30% traffic, us-west-1). Early perf numbers look good; one hot path regressed for 2048-token workloads — mitigation in flight.
- Dedicated beta: two customers onboarded to dedicated pools (billing + infra smoke tests passed).
- Private deployment pilot: first on-prem install scheduled for next week (legal & security checklist completed).
- Notable SRE alert: autoscaler oscillation in us-west-2 causing transient request throttling; immediate mitigation applied.

2) Signals / metrics (rolling 24–72h windows)
- P95 generation latency (hosted API): baseline 210ms -> canary cohort 230ms (investigation ongoing)
- Error rate (5xx): global 0.7% (spike in us-west-2 to 2.4% during autoscaler incidents)
- Token cost per 1k (estimate): stable vs last week; slight improvement from batching configs for chat routes
- Throughput: Dedicated pools operating at 78% avg utilization

3) Current blockers and asks (owner + ask)
- KV cache regression on long-sequence paths (owner: Aisha Khan) — temporary workaround: disable prefix caching for model-x in canary; ask: eng-serving-runtime to triage and propose a kernel fallback by EOD Thu (Jira ENG-801).
- Autoscaler flapping (owner: SRE lead, Miguel Ortega) — mitigation: bumped scale cooldown; ask: platform-engineering to add additional health-check metric (kv-cache hit ratio) into scaling decision by next sprint.
- Dedicated pool burst policy docs missing (owner: Priya Desai) — ask product to publish short runbook + failure-mode checklist for on-call.

4) Release & rollout notes (runtime v1.12)
- Canary: 30% traffic in us-west-1 and eu-central-1. Observability hooks added (token-level traces, KV cache metrics).
- Known regressions: increased decode time for long sequences when kernel A selected (tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456).
- Rollback criteria: sustained p95 > 300ms or error rate > 1.5% for 15m window.

5) Cross-team updates (one-line from each area)
- Serving runtime: Aisha — debugging KV cache kernel selection; will push hotfix if root cause isolated.
- Platform infra: Evan — autoscaler cooldown bump applied; adding canary-specific autoscale profile.
- Console & tooling: Hana (PM) — new per-route latency charts staged in canary console; feedback welcome.
- DevEx: Priya — updated quickstart for dedicated pools; added troubleshooting notes.

6) Incident recap (SRE brief)
- What happened: repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles in us-west-2 caused capacity holes and request throttling between 09:12–09:46 UTC (6/8).
- Root cause (investigation in progress): aggressive cooldown + noisy health check on KV-temperature metric.
- Immediate mitigation: extended cooldown, temporarily increased min replicas, suppressed noisy health-check signal.
- Next steps: more robust health aggregation (owner: Miguel), postmortem to be published by Friday (Jira ENG-789).

7) Action items (owner — due)
- Aisha: produce kernel selection experiment results and test harness by Thu 2026-06-11.
- Miguel: final postmortem and remediation plan published by 2026-06-11.
- Priya: Dedicated runbook draft (internal) by Mon 2026-06-15.
- Platform-eng: add autoscaler metric hook (kv-cache hit ratio) to scaling decisions — proposal by next planning sync (2026-06-23).

8) Risks and horizon scanning
- If runtime regressions persist on long-sequence workloads, customer-visible latency may breach SLO for chat/assistant apps — contingency plan: route long sequences to quantized model variant until kernel fixes land.
- Dedicated demand: forecast shows +25% committed cores next quarter; capacity planning meeting scheduled with infra finance.

9) Q&A highlights from the floor
- Q: Are we pausing the canary? A: Not yet — hotfix path prioritized; we will pause if rollback criteria hit.
- Q: Is dedicated billing impacted? A: No customer invoices affected; billing flow validated in beta.

10) Shoutouts + wins
- Shoutout to SRE (Miguel, Lina) for fast mitigation during the autoscaler incident.
- Win: Priya and Solutions Eng for smoothing Dedicated onboarding for two early customers this week.

Appendix: useful links and tickets
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456
- Postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-789
- Release notes draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/1.12+Release+Notes

Notes for next sync: keep canary instrumentation tighter (per-route traces + KV cache heatmap), finalize rollback automation, capacity planning for Dedicated Q3 commitments.
